chapters.title: Start here
chapters.summary: Bursara brings student fees, bills, receipts and unpaid balances into one workspace. This guide follows the application’s financial workflow.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Open https://app.bursara.com. Choose English or French in the language selector. Your choice is remembered across the website and application. Sign in with the account supplied by your institution.
Create a course and its priced units, then enrol a student. A course is the full programme; a unit is a priced year, subject or module.
Save an invoice draft and review it. An authorised user selects Post invoice. Record the money received as a payment draft, then select Post payment when authorised.
Open the student account to review posted balances. Drafts do not affect the account totals. Use About this screen for a short explanation and a link to the relevant guide.

image.alt: Start here in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: BURARA CHILRENS ACADEMY is a protected shared demonstration. Use fictional learners, contacts and simulated payments. Other testers can see demonstration records.
This guide covers school financial administration. Attendance, check-in/check-out and timetables are not included.

chapters.title: Understand the money words
chapters.summary: A few everyday terms make the rest of the screens easier to follow.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: A bill or invoice says what a student or their responsible party owes. It can cover the whole year even when payment will come in smaller parts.
A receipt acknowledges money already received. Recording a bill alone does not mean the school has received money.
An allocation applies a received payment to a particular bill. The bill then shows a lower outstanding balance.
An instalment is one scheduled amount and due date within a bill. Outstanding includes every unpaid amount; overdue includes only amounts whose due dates have passed.
Unapplied credit is money received for a student that has not yet been used against a bill. A fee credit reduces a charge; a refund returns unused money.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: Example: a MUR 120,000 annual bill paid in twelve monthly instalments still starts as one MUR 120,000 bill. A MUR 25,000 allocated payment leaves MUR 95,000 outstanding. The overdue amount depends on the instalment dates and the selected balance date.
A bill, receipt and fee credit are different financial records even when an institution chooses a combined invoice/receipt workflow.

chapters.title: Sign in and sign out
chapters.summary: Sign in to reach the workspace your administrator has assigned to you.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: If you have registered a passkey, select Sign in with passkey and follow your device’s verification prompt. Otherwise enter Email address and Password, then select Sign in.
If the password method opens Verify your sign-in, enter the current code from your authenticator app or one unused recovery code. Select Verify and sign in.
Institution users arrive at their own institution. Platform staff arrive at Client institutions. A verified passkey signs you in without a separate authenticator-code step.
If the email or password is incorrect, check the spelling and try again. After five failed attempts for the same account and connection, wait the number of seconds shown.
When finished, select Sign out at the bottom of the navigation menu. On a shared computer, close the browser after signing out.

image.alt: Sign in and sign out in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: Your institution administrator creates ordinary user accounts and can set a new password through Users & permissions. A password reset does not remove an enabled authenticator. Bursara does not provide a self-service forgotten-password screen.

The shared demonstration login is protected. Its password cannot be changed and it cannot enrol passkeys or time-based one-time passwords. Private platform staff credentials are never included in this guide.

chapters.title: Passkeys, verification and recovery
chapters.summary: Sign-in security protects your own login. These options are available to institution users and platform staff; the shared demonstration login stays locked.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Open Sign-in security. Enter a Passkey name and select Add a passkey to register a device.
Confirm it’s you asks for Current password and, if enabled, an Authenticator or recovery code. Select Continue and follow your device prompt.
For app codes, select Set up authenticator app, confirm your identity, then privately scan the QR code or enter the setup key in your authenticator app.
Enter Code from your authenticator app and select Enable authenticator. Password sign-in now needs a current app code or unused recovery code.
Save the eight recovery codes privately using copy or download, then select I’ve saved these codes. Each works once. Replace recovery codes invalidates the old set.
A verified passkey signs you in without a separate app code. Remove a retired key beside its name, or use Turn off authenticator to disable app codes, confirming your identity when asked.

image.alt: Sign-in security controls for a fictional ordinary local user.
image.caption: Set up the authenticator only on your own ordinary account.

image.alt: Passkey name and Add a passkey controls.
image.caption: Give the device a recognisable name before registering its passkey.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: Keep setup keys and recovery codes private. If all sign-in methods are unavailable, contact your institution administrator or Bursara support.
The protected demonstration cannot enable these methods. An administrator changing your password does not remove existing passkeys or verification.

chapters.title: Find your way around
chapters.summary: The left menu groups the daily work. The floating help control explains the screen you are viewing.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Use Students for learners and their individual accounts. Use Courses & units for programmes and their fees.
Use Billing for posted charges and Payments for received money and receipts.
Use Debtors to follow unpaid fees. Reports contains currency summaries, the financial control journal and the balance export.
Select About this screen at the lower right. Read the explanation, then select the same control again to close it.
Open Sign-in security to protect your own login. If another menu item or action is missing, ask your administrator whether your user has the relevant permission.

image.alt: Find your way around in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: Saving or editing a draft does not affect financial totals. Posting an invoice or payment, allocating credit, issuing a fee credit or recording a refund does change the account.
Tables use a ledger layout and highlight rows on hover. Use the English/Français selector to change language; your choice is remembered.

chapters.title: Read the overview
chapters.summary: The overview gives a quick account position for one currency and one date.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Choose Balance date. The figures use financial records up to that date, so changing it lets you review an earlier position.
Choose Display currency. Each currency has its own figures; selecting USD does not convert every MUR transaction into dollars.
Read the four totals: Fees billed, Payments received, Outstanding and Overdue.
Look at unapplied student credit below the totals. This is received money still available to apply to a student's bills.
Open a document in Recent bills or Recent collections, or use Create invoice draft and Create payment draft when your permissions allow them.

image.alt: Read the overview in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: Only posted financial records affect these figures. Saved drafts are excluded. Outstanding and overdue answer different questions. A future instalment is outstanding but is not overdue. An instalment due today becomes overdue only after that day has passed.
The overview is a starting point. Open the relevant bill, student account or report to understand a particular figure.

chapters.title: Create a course
chapters.summary: A course is the complete programme, such as High School or BSc Biomedical Sciences.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Open Courses & units and select New course.
Enter Course name in language that school staff will recognise.
Enter a short Code, such as HS. Codes must be unique within your institution.
Optionally enter a Description, then select Create course.
Add the priced units next. Creating the course by itself does not bill any student.

image.alt: Create a course in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: For annual school billing, create one High School course and Year 1 to Year 4 units. For university billing, create the programme as the course and subjects as its units.

To correct an existing course, select Edit course, change its name, code or description and save. To change a unit, select Edit unit. Existing posted document lines keep their saved prices and descriptions.

chapters.title: Set a fixed unit fee
chapters.summary: Use a fixed fee when the price applies to the entire unit, such as one school year.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: In Courses & units, select Add unit. Choose its Course.
Enter Unit name and a unique Code. For example, use Year 1 and Y1.
Enter Price and choose Currency. Enter amounts as numbers without currency symbols or thousands separators.
Choose Fixed unit fee in Price basis. For a whole-year fee, leave Credits / weight as 1.
Select Save unit. The unit will appear under its course and can be selected when enrolling a student.

image.alt: Set a fixed unit fee in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: Example: Year 1 at a fixed MUR 120,000 price gives a MUR 120,000 fee for quantity 1, before discount or tax.

Use Edit unit to update the name, code, price, currency, price basis or credit weight. Changes apply to future selections. Review saved invoice drafts separately; posted lines keep their original amounts. Different unit currencies require separate invoices.

chapters.title: Set a fee per credit
chapters.summary: Use a per-credit fee when the unit charge depends on its credit weight.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Select Add unit and choose the programme in Course.
Enter the unit name and code, such as Cell Biology and BIO101.
Enter the price for one credit in Price, then choose Currency.
Choose Per credit in Price basis. Enter the number of credits in Credits / weight.
Select Save unit. When this enrolled unit is selected on a bill, Bursara fills the quantity with its credit weight.

image.alt: Set a fee per credit in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: Example: a unit with a USD 250 price per credit and a weight of 3 credits gives a USD 750 fee before discount or tax.

The posted bill uses the quantity and unit price shown on its fee line. Check them before posting. Unit prices support up to five decimal places and credit weights up to three; the final amount is rounded to the currency's normal precision.

chapters.title: Enrol a student
chapters.summary: Enrolment connects a learner, the party responsible for paying and the units that may be billed.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Open Students and select Enrol student. Enter Student name and a unique Student reference.
Enter the Debtor / billing contact: the person or organisation responsible for the fees. Choose Parent / guardian, Student or Sponsor / employer under Responsible party.
Optionally enter a student email, contact phone and billing address. Use fictional details while testing Bursara.
Choose Course. Tick the Billable units in which the student is enrolled.
Select Enrol student. Bursara opens the Student account. Check the learner, programme and billing contact.

image.alt: Enrol a student in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: Units must belong to the chosen course. Enrol a learner in a priced unit before selecting it on their invoice; a custom fee can also be entered directly.

To update the learner, select Edit on the Students row or Edit student in the account. Review contacts, programme and selected units, then save. The student reference stays unique. Posted documents retain their original student details. Attendance and timetables are not included.

chapters.title: Edit courses, units and students
chapters.summary: Keep the catalogue and learner records current without rewriting posted documents.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: In Courses & units, choose Edit course to change the name, unique code or description. Save the course.
Choose Edit unit to change its name, code, price, currency, price basis or credits. An enrolled unit cannot be moved to another course; create a new unit instead.
In Students choose Edit, or open an account and choose Edit student. Review the reference, contact details, responsible party, course and selected units, then save.
When changing the course, select only units belonging to the new course. Review the selected units before saving.
Existing drafts do not silently take new unit prices. Open Edit draft and review its lines. Posted invoices and receipts retain their saved amounts and student details.

image.alt: Course and unit editing actions in Bursara.
image.caption: Use the edit action on the record you intend to change.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: Manage courses and fees controls catalogue changes. Manage students controls learner changes. An edit never grants access to another institution.
There is no deletion or student promotion workflow here. Verify references and contacts before saving.

chapters.title: Use a student account
chapters.summary: The student account brings one learner's bills and receipts together.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Open Students, search by name, reference or debtor, and select the student name or open arrow.
Check the learner and billing-contact details. These identify the account being reviewed.
Read the outstanding amount and unapplied credit for each currency. Different currencies stay separate.
Use the Fee register to open a bill. Use the Receipt register to open a receipt.
Select Create invoice draft, Create payment draft or Print statement as needed. Your permissions determine which actions are available.

image.alt: Use a student account in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: The student account is useful when a parent or sponsor asks what remains to be paid. Open the individual bill to see its monthly due dates and exactly how payments have been applied.
Unapplied credit is shown separately from outstanding fees. It does not settle a bill until you explicitly apply it.

chapters.title: Choose the billing workflow
chapters.summary: Choose how the charge and the collection should be recorded before posting.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Open Billing and select Create invoice draft. Choose the Student and Billing workflow.
Choose Bill first, collect later for a charge that will be collected separately. Choose Assessed fees with instalments for an assessment with scheduled due amounts.
Choose Receive full payment and issue only when the entire charge has already been received. Its payment method and reference are saved with the draft.
Select Save draft, then review the draft document. Select Edit draft to correct it before posting.
An authorised user selects Post invoice. For the combined workflow, this posts the invoice and its full payment together; otherwise record payments separately.

image.alt: Choose the billing workflow in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: Saving a draft requires Create and edit invoice drafts. Posting requires Post invoices; the combined workflow also requires Post payments. Saving a draft does not bill a student or acknowledge received money.

A draft receives a permanent SO-00001 creation reference. Its final INV000001 number is assigned only when posted. Draft edits consume no final invoice numbers. SO and PO are creation references, not sales or purchase orders.

chapters.title: Review, edit and post a draft
chapters.summary: A saved draft is a preparation step. Posting makes the financial document effective.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Open Billing or Payments and find the SO or PO creation reference. Use the Draft status filter if needed.
Open the draft and review learner, dates, currency, amounts and fee lines or proposed allocations. No account balance has changed yet.
With Create and edit invoice drafts or Create and edit payment drafts, choose Edit draft. Make the correction and save. The permanent creation reference stays the same.
An authorised user selects Post invoice or Post payment. The final INV or REC number is assigned only now, and balances and the journal are updated.
If a payment allocation is refused because another operation settled the bill, edit the draft to match the current balance. Search the register before creating a replacement.

image.alt: Edit draft and Post invoice actions on a saved invoice draft.
image.caption: Creation and posting have separate permissions. The draft keeps its SO reference after posting.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: Posted documents cannot be edited. Use a separate approved credit or refund where supported. Repeating a post request does not create another financial document.
A submitted fiscal draft cannot be edited, even when its provider result is rejected or uncertain. An unsubmitted prepared snapshot is invalidated when its draft changes.

chapters.title: Create an annual school bill
chapters.summary: Bill the whole school year once and then collect the money over time.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Create the bill, select the student and choose Bill first, collect later. Enter Issue date and Service period, such as Academic year 2027.
Choose the school year in Enrolled unit. Check Description, Quantity / credits and Unit price. Use Add line for another charge.
Confirm Currency. When it differs from the functional currency, enter the rate requested by the form. Review discounts and tax.
Enter First due date and Monthly instalments, then select Save draft. The draft has an SO creation reference and does not affect outstanding fees.
Review the saved document. Use Edit draft to correct it. An authorised user selects Post invoice to assign its final invoice number and create the charge.

image.alt: Create an annual school bill in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: MUR 120,000 with quantity 1 is one annual fee. Twelve instalments change when it is due, not the fee total.
Posted records are immutable. Correct an unpaid charge using an authorised separate fee credit rather than changing the original invoice.

chapters.title: Set monthly instalments
chapters.summary: The schedule says when parts of a bill fall due. It does not create extra invoices or extra fees.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: In the invoice draft form, enter First due date on or after Issue date.
Choose Monthly instalments. Use One payment due when the full charge is due on one date.
Add Notes, select Save draft and inspect the proposed schedule. Use Edit draft if the dates or amounts need correction.
Select Post invoice when authorised. Check Payment schedule on the posted document. The final invoice number is assigned at this point.
Save and post payment drafts as money arrives. Confirmed allocations pay the earliest unpaid instalments first.

image.alt: Set monthly instalments in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: MUR 120,000 over twelve instalments gives MUR 10,000 each. Bursara distributes rounding remainders so the schedule always equals the exact invoice total.
Monthly dates retain the chosen day where possible: 31 January is followed by 28 or 29 February, then 31 March. Automatic repeat invoice generation is not included.

chapters.title: Bill university units
chapters.summary: Use one or more enrolled units instead of a whole-year school fee.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Create an invoice draft for the learner. Enter Service period, such as Semester 1 / 2027.
Choose an Enrolled unit. For a per-credit fee, check the filled Quantity / credits and price for one credit.
Check Currency and the requested Rate. Add further units in the same currency with Add line.
Enter the due schedule and select Save draft. Open Edit draft to correct the subjects, quantity or prices before posting.
Select Post invoice when authorised. Confirm its final number and posted schedule. Create another invoice for units in a different currency.

image.alt: Bill university units in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: Three credits at USD 250 give a USD 750 line. A fixed USD 400 laboratory fee can be added as a second line with quantity 1.
The invoice saves its own descriptions, prices, student details and rate. Later catalogue or student edits do not rewrite posted documents.

chapters.title: Receive full payment and issue together
chapters.summary: Use this workflow when the entire fee is paid at the time you issue the document.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Create an invoice draft and choose Receive full payment and issue in Billing workflow.
Complete the student, dates, currency and fee lines. Select Payment method and enter Payment reference where available.
Select Save draft. Review its SO creation reference, fee total and proposed payment details. No charge or receipt is posted yet.
Only when the full amount has really arrived, an authorised user selects Post invoice. This requires both Post invoices and Post payments.
Open the resulting invoice and receipt. Check the final INV and REC numbers and zero Outstanding balance.

image.alt: Receive full payment and issue together in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: Posting completes the full invoice and payment together. Repeating the post action does not create another charge or receipt.
For a partial collection, post an ordinary invoice and prepare a separate payment draft. Bursara records a payment method but does not initiate bank transfers or charge cards.

chapters.title: Read a posted invoice
chapters.summary: The posted invoice is the record of the charge, its payments and its unpaid balance.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: In Billing, open the invoice number. Check the institution, student, billing contact, date and service period.
Review each line: description, quantity, unit price, discount, tax and amount.
Read Total fees, Payments applied, Credits and Outstanding. Check the Payment schedule below.
Use Receive payment to prepare a collection, or Credit outstanding fees for an approved reduction of unpaid charges.

image.alt: Read a posted invoice in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Check the institution, student and final invoice number.

image.alt: Invoice financial summary.
image.caption: Read the posted totals and remaining balance.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: The permanent SO reference stays alongside the INV number assigned at posting. Outstanding includes future unpaid instalments. Posted invoices cannot be edited: use a separate credit where supported. Fiscal documents require their local correction process.

chapters.title: Record a partial payment
chapters.summary: Record only the money actually received, then apply it to the student's bill.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Open an unpaid invoice and select Receive payment. The student and bill are preselected.
Enter the Amount received. If MUR 25,000 arrived, enter 25000 even when the full bill is MUR 120,000.
Check Received date, Method, Payer and Reference. Use a bank transfer only after it is confirmed, or Cleared cheque only after it has cleared.
In Allocate to bills, leave the correct bill selected and enter the portion to apply in Apply (MUR).
Select Save draft. Review the saved payment, use Edit draft if needed, then select Post payment when authorised. Open the bill again and check its new Outstanding amount.

image.alt: Record a partial payment in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: A payment draft receives a permanent PO-00001 creation reference but changes no balance. Post payment assigns REC000001 and records the money and allocations. Create and edit payment drafts and Post payments are separate rights.

MUR 25,000 applied to a posted MUR 120,000 bill leaves MUR 95,000 outstanding. Posting rechecks the latest invoice balance; if another receipt has settled it, edit the draft allocations before trying again.

chapters.title: Allocate one payment to bills
chapters.summary: An allocation tells Bursara which unpaid charge the received money should settle.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Open Payments and select Create payment draft. Choose the student and fill in the received amount, date, currency and method.
Under Allocate to bills, tick each bill that this payment should help settle.
Enter the amount to apply for each selected bill. The total used from the payment must not exceed Amount received.
Leave a bill unticked when this payment is not intended for it. Any unused received money remains unapplied student credit.
Select Save draft. Review the saved payment, use Edit draft if needed, then select Post payment when authorised. Review Applied to fees on the receipt and follow an invoice link to check its balance.

image.alt: Allocate one payment to bills in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: 1 Select the bill that this payment should settle. 2 Enter the amount to apply. The payment must have enough money available.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: A payment can be applied to several bills for the same student. It cannot be applied to another student's bill or to another institution.
For one currency, the applied bill amount and the amount used from the payment are the same. For different currencies, you must enter both sides, as explained in the next procedure.

chapters.title: Receive a payment in another currency
chapters.summary: Record the currency received and the amount of the bill that it settles as two separate amounts.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Open Receive a payment and choose the payment Currency. Enter Amount received in that currency.
Enter the Rate requested by the form. Read the label carefully: Rate: 1 USD in MUR means how many MUR equal one USD.
Tick the bill being paid. Enter Apply (MUR) as the amount to remove from the MUR bill.
Enter Uses (USD) as the part of the USD payment used for that allocation.
Check both amounts and the rate, then select Save draft, review it and select Post payment when authorised. Review the currencies shown in Applied to fees.

image.alt: Receive a payment in another currency in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: Example: the school receives USD 100 and agrees that this settles MUR 4,600 of a bill. Enter 100 received, 4600 in Apply (MUR), 100 in Uses (USD), and the appropriate rate of 46.

Bursara does not fetch exchange rates automatically. Your institution must supply the correct rate and agreed settlement amounts. MUR, USD and most supported currencies use two decimal places; JPY uses none and KWD uses three.

chapters.title: Record an advance payment
chapters.summary: Keep money received before it is assigned to a bill as unapplied student credit.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Open Payments and select Create payment draft. Select the correct Student and Payer.
Enter Amount received, Currency, Received date, Method and any Reference.
Under Allocate to bills, leave every bill unticked. If the student has no unpaid bills, the form explains that the money will be held as credit.
Select Save draft. Review it, then select Post payment when authorised. Review Unapplied credit on the receipt.
Keep the receipt reference. Later, open it to apply available credit to a bill or refund unused money.

image.alt: Record an advance payment in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: Save and post an advance even when there is no invoice. Posting records received money as unapplied credit; it settles no invoice until explicitly allocated.

The PO creation reference stays with the payment after its REC receipt number is assigned. For a payment received before an invoice date, leave it unapplied first, then apply credit with a valid later date.

chapters.title: Apply existing student credit
chapters.summary: Use an earlier unapplied payment against an outstanding bill without recording the money twice.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Open the original receipt from Payments or the student's Receipt register.
If credit remains and a same-currency bill is unpaid, select Apply student credit.
Choose the Outstanding invoice. Enter Apply amount (MUR), or the currency shown.
Enter Allocation date. It cannot be earlier than the original payment, the bill or a refund already recorded against that payment.
Select Apply credit to bill. Check that the receipt's unapplied credit and the bill's outstanding amount both decrease.

image.alt: Apply existing student credit in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: This is an application of money already received. Do not use Receive payment again for the same money.

Bursara applies existing credit to bills in the same currency and for the same student. If the action is absent, check the receipt's available credit, the student's unpaid bills and your Post payments and apply credit permission.

chapters.title: Refund unused credit
chapters.summary: Record money returned from the part of a payment that has not been applied to bills.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Open the receipt and check its Unapplied credit. Select Refund unused credit.
Enter the refund Amount in the currency shown. It cannot exceed the available unapplied credit.
Enter Date. The refund cannot predate the original payment.
Enter a clear Reason, then select Record refund.
Confirm that Refunded increases and Unapplied credit decreases on the receipt. Keep the real-world payment reference in your own process as needed.

image.alt: Refund unused credit in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: This records a refund that your institution has arranged. It does not send money to a bank or card.

Only unused credit can be refunded in Bursara. Returning money that has already been applied to a bill needs a fuller reversal workflow and is not supported here. Do not record a negative payment to work around that limit.

chapters.title: Reduce an outstanding fee
chapters.summary: A fee credit reduces a charge that remains unpaid, for example an approved scholarship adjustment.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Open the invoice and select Credit outstanding fees. The action requires credit/refund permission.
Enter Amount in the invoice currency. It cannot exceed the current outstanding balance.
Enter Date, on or after the bill issue date and any payment already applied to the bill.
Enter a clear Reason, then select Record credit.
Check the invoice's Credits and Outstanding figures. The original charge remains visible and the credit appears as a separate record.

image.alt: Reduce an outstanding fee in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: A fee credit does not return cash. To record money returned from an unused advance, use Refund unused credit on its receipt.

Credit is applied to the latest unpaid scheduled amounts first. If the bill has a fiscal document, Bursara blocks this core credit action because the local e-invoicing module must handle the fiscal correction. Fiscal credit notes are not implemented in Bursara.

chapters.title: Read and print a receipt
chapters.summary: The receipt shows money received, the bills paid from it and any money still unused.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Open Payments and select a receipt number. Check the payer, student, received date, method and reference.
Read Amount received. Under Applied to fees, follow an invoice number to inspect its charge and outstanding balance.
Check Refunded and Unapplied credit. These explain why some of the received amount may no longer be available to allocate.
Select Print / PDF. In your browser's print window, choose a printer or Save as PDF.
Check the print preview before saving or printing. The navigation and action buttons are left out of the printed document.

image.alt: Read and print a receipt in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: Demonstration documents are marked as testing documents. They must not be used as real tax invoices or real payment acknowledgements.
An institution may use the combined invoice/receipt workflow when charging and collecting together. The receipt register still records the money received.

chapters.title: Print a student statement
chapters.summary: Use a statement to review one student's charges and receipts together.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Open Students and select the learner. Confirm the correct name and reference.
Review outstanding fees and unapplied credit for each currency, then review the Fee register and Receipt register.
Select Print statement. Choose your printer or Save as PDF in the browser print window.
Check the preview and page breaks. Save or print the statement using your institution's usual document-sharing process.

image.alt: Print a student statement in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: The statement reflects the current student account. It is not a new invoice or a new receipt and does not change the balance.
To explain a particular instalment or payment, open the related invoice or receipt as well. Use Debtors or Reports with Balance date when you need an institution-wide position at an earlier date.

chapters.title: Follow outstanding and overdue fees
chapters.summary: Debtors helps staff follow up the fees that remain unpaid.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Open Debtors. Select Balance date to choose the date of the position you want to inspect.
Choose Display currency. Read Outstanding fees and Overdue instalments.
Use Search records to find a student, debtor or invoice. The table shows open bills in the selected currency.
Open a bill to inspect its Payment schedule and Outstanding amount.
If money has arrived, use Receive payment. If an approved unpaid charge must be reduced, use Credit outstanding fees.

image.alt: Follow outstanding and overdue fees in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: Only posted financial records affect these figures. Saved drafts are excluded. Outstanding includes unpaid future instalments. Overdue includes scheduled amounts due before the chosen date. For example, a MUR 95,000 balance is not necessarily MUR 95,000 overdue.

Bursara provides the open-balance view. Automatic reminder emails, collection campaigns and a separate collection-case workflow are not included. Follow your institution's communication process when contacting the responsible party.

chapters.title: Review and export balances
chapters.summary: Reports gives a currency summary and a spreadsheet-friendly list of invoice balances.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Open Reports and choose Balance date. Use the same date when comparing the report with Debtors.
Read Balances by currency. Billed, collected, outstanding and overdue amounts are separated by currency.
Select Export balances. Your browser downloads bursara-open-items.csv.
Open the CSV in your spreadsheet application. Check the invoice, student, debtor, currency, total, paid, credit, balance and overdue columns.
Keep the chosen date with the exported file so another person knows which position was reviewed.

image.alt: Review and export balances in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: Only posted financial records affect these figures. Saved drafts are excluded. A CSV is a table of values, not a formatted PDF. Your spreadsheet may ask how to interpret dates, numbers or the comma separator. Collected shows the money originally received before any refunds; it is not a net-cash figure.
Bursara does not connect to an external accounting platform. Use this export for review and testing; establish the full reporting and accounting process before using Bursara for live operations.

chapters.title: Understand the financial control journal
chapters.summary: The journal is a supporting view for staff who need to trace the financial effect of a posting.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Open Reports and scroll to Financial control journal.
Read Date and Source to identify whether an entry came from an invoice, payment, credit, refund or application of existing credit.
Read Account to understand the type of movement. Movement uses the institution's functional currency.
Positive amounts are debits and negative amounts are credits. The movements belonging to each posting should add to zero.
Use the relevant invoice or receipt to investigate a source record. Ask the institution's finance lead if the treatment is unclear.

image.alt: Understand the financial control journal in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: Only posted financial records affect these figures. Saved drafts are excluded. This view shows the latest 100 postings. It is a financial control trail, not a complete general ledger, statutory accounts package or accounting-platform integration.
Ordinary daily users can work through bills, receipts and student accounts without reading journal entries. This screen is available only when report permission is granted.

chapters.title: Create an institution user
chapters.summary: An authorised administrator can create a login for another member of the institution's team.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Open Users & permissions and select New user.
Enter Full name and Login email. Each person should have their own login.
Enter a password of at least twelve characters. Share access privately.
Tick the needed rights. Grant draft creation and posting separately: a cashier may prepare payment drafts while a supervisor posts them.
Select Save user and rights. Ask the person to sign in and check the expected screens and actions.

image.alt: Create an institution user in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: Every institution user is confined to that institution. A new ordinary user cannot use the platform staff institution-switching screen.
Users who can manage other users can assign powerful permissions, so grant that right carefully. The protected demonstration login cannot be edited or have its password changed.

chapters.title: Set the right permissions
chapters.summary: Bursara checks these permissions whenever someone tries an action.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Open Users & permissions and select Edit permissions for an ordinary user.
Manage students allows creating and editing learners. Manage courses and fees allows creating and editing programmes and units.
Create and edit invoice drafts allows saving and correcting drafts. Post invoices separately authorises posting. Create and edit payment drafts and Post payments follow the same separation.
Receive full payment and issue requires both posting rights. Issue credits and refunds authorises separate corrections. Review report, module, settings and user-management rights individually.
Select Save user and rights. Check the user sees the expected actions. A draft creator can leave posting to another authorised person.

image.alt: Set the right permissions in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: 1 Create and edit payment drafts. 2 Post payments and apply credit. Grant these rights separately to match the person’s responsibilities.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: Permissions do not change which institution the person belongs to. An empty checkbox selection grants none of the listed action rights. Your account cannot remove its own user-management access here.

To change an ordinary user password, enter a new password; leave it blank to keep the current one. This does not remove passkeys or an enabled authenticator. The demonstration account remains protected.

chapters.title: Review institution settings
chapters.summary: Settings contains the institution identity, address, country and timezone.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Open Settings. Check Institution name, Country code, Timezone and Address.
For an ordinary client institution, make the permitted changes and select Save institution.
Read the functional currency shown near the top. This is set when the institution is created and cannot be changed here.
For the shared demonstration, read the protected-identity notice. The identity fields and Save institution action are disabled.

image.alt: Review institution settings in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: Use a two-letter country code such as MU and a recognised timezone such as Indian/Mauritius. The timezone determines the institution's current date for account views.
The locked demonstration protects its name and login from changes by testers. It can still be used to try ordinary synthetic school-finance workflows.

chapters.title: Platform staff: create a client
chapters.summary: Platform staff can create isolated workspaces for schools and other learning institutions.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Sign in with an authorised platform staff account. On Client institutions, select New institution.
Enter Institution name, Country code, Functional currency and Timezone. Choose the functional currency carefully because it is fixed for that institution.
Enter Administrator name and Administrator email. Enter a temporary password of at least twelve characters.
Select Create institution. Bursara creates the workspace and its first administrator together.
Share the administrator's access privately. Select Enter workspace on the new institution to help with its initial setup.

image.alt: Platform staff: create a client in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

image.alt: Temporary password field and Create institution button highlighted in the institution form.
image.caption: Lower-form detail: enter a private temporary password of at least 12 characters, then select Create institution. No password is shown.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: The first administrator belongs only to this new institution. Other schools' students and financial records are not copied. Share account access privately.

chapters.title: Platform staff: enter and leave a school
chapters.summary: Support access lets authorised platform staff work inside a chosen institution without sharing its users' passwords.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: On Client institutions, find the correct institution and select Enter workspace.
Check the institution name in the menu and the Support access banner before making any change.
Perform the authorised support task. Platform staff can use all actions in that institution, subject to demonstration protections.
Select Exit institution in the banner to return to Client institutions.
When finished supporting clients, select Sign out.

image.alt: Platform staff: enter and leave a school in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: Entry and exit are recorded as support sessions. Signing out also closes the active support session. Financial records posted during support retain the staff user as the actor.

Take particular care when two client names look similar. Always check the visible institution name before posting a bill, collection or correction. The shared demonstration's identity and login remain protected even during support access.

chapters.title: Optional Mauritius EBS module
chapters.summary: EBS is an optional Mauritius fiscal-reporting module. Core billing works without it.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: For a Mauritius institution with module permission, open Modules. The shared demonstration cannot submit external fiscal documents.
Tick Enable EBS sandbox only with appropriate test access. Choose Report when: Invoice is raised or Payment is received.
Choose the document stage for preparation: Draft or Posted. Posted is the normal default. This is independent of whether the event is an invoice or payment.
Enter Sandbox API key and select Save module. Leave the key blank on later saves to retain it.
Review the chosen event, stage and module limitations. Saving a draft or posting money does not automatically prepare or send anything.

image.alt: Optional Mauritius EBS module in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: 1 Enable the test module. 2 Choose the reporting event. 3 Choose Draft or Posted document stage independently.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: The module uses the EBS test environment. Saved credentials are encrypted and are not shown again. Never share them in screenshots or support examples.
Only Mauritius institutions can enable EBS. The core financial workflows are independent of it. No accounting platform integration is included.

chapters.title: Prepare and review a sandbox fiscal document
chapters.summary: Preparing a fiscal document and submitting it are separate actions in Bursara.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: In Modules, select the eligible Invoice and, in payment mode, its allocated Payment. Eligibility follows the saved event and Draft or Posted stage.
Select Prepare sandbox document. This saves a snapshot in Fiscal register; it does not send it to EBS.
Select Review. Check the institution, amounts, currency, event and the separate fiscal reference. EBS uses its own continuous fiscal numbering; SO and PO remain creation references.
An authorised tester with test credentials may select Submit to sandbox. Ordinary billing exercises need no submission.
For a queued reference, use Refresh status. Reconcile an Unknown result with EBS before retrying or preparing another reference.

image.alt: Prepare and review a sandbox fiscal document in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: 1 Select the invoice. 2 Prepare the sandbox document locally.

image.alt: Prepared sandbox document with Review and Submit to sandbox highlighted.
image.caption: A prepared document is ready for review. Submit to sandbox is a separate action; it was not used to make this guide.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: An unsubmitted prepared snapshot is invalidated if its financial draft changes, so prepare it again after review. A submitted fiscal draft is locked against financial editing, including rejected or uncertain submissions.

Current service lines support undiscounted exempt or 15% charges. Payment reporting supports allocated untaxed tuition. Prepared does not mean accepted; Queued is pending, Accepted is success and Unknown needs reconciliation. Live submissions and fiscal credit notes are not included.

chapters.title: Use Bursara on a smaller screen
chapters.summary: The same financial workflows are available in the responsive browser interface.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: On a phone-sized screen, select Open menu near the upper left.
Choose the screen you need, such as Students, Billing or Payments. Use Close menu if you want to return without navigating.
Swipe horizontally inside a wide ledger table to see columns that do not fit. Opening a document gives a clearer view of its full details.
In a long form, scroll to review every fee line, date and amount before posting.
Use About this screen for a short reminder. For printing or detailed multi-line entry, a larger screen may be easier.

image.alt: Use Bursara on a smaller screen in Bursara, with numbered controls highlighted.
image.caption: Numbered outlines identify the controls described in the steps. Screens show fictional demonstration records.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: Bursara is a web application. It does not require a separate mobile-app installation, and it does not include offline operation.
Use the browser's normal zoom and text controls when necessary, then verify the whole financial document before sharing or printing.

chapters.title: Solve common problems
chapters.summary: Use the message on the screen to decide the next step. Avoid creating a second transaction to solve an uncertain first attempt.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Cannot sign in: check email and password, or use a registered passkey. If Verify your sign-in appears, use your authenticator app or an unused recovery code. After repeated failures, wait for the displayed delay. Ask the institution administrator for account help. If a verification code was just used, wait for the next code in your app.
Missing button or access denied: ask an administrator to review your permission checkboxes. Client users cannot enter another institution.
Unit missing from a bill: check the student's chosen course and enrolled units. Units from another course or another currency cannot be silently combined.
Payment will not post: check decimal precision, positive amounts, dates and allocations. Applied amounts cannot exceed the bill or available payment.
Credit or refund blocked: a fee credit cannot exceed unpaid fees; a refund cannot exceed unused student credit. Fiscal documents need their country-specific e-invoicing correction process.
Unknown fiscal result: stop and reconcile the original reference. Do not submit it again just because a response was slow.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: If you are unsure whether a bill or payment was posted, first search Billing or Payments and open the student account. Check for the existing document before trying another transaction.
When reporting a problem, give the screen name, document number, steps taken, expected outcome and exact visible message. Use fictional records and remove confidential information from screenshots.

chapters.title: Help, boundaries and quick reference
chapters.summary: Use this final page as a short reminder and a route to support.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Institution: one school, college or learning organisation with its own isolated records.
Course: the whole programme. Unit: a priced year, subject, module or other part of that programme.
Debtor: the student, parent, guardian, employer or sponsor responsible for paying.
Functional currency: the institution's main reporting currency. Document currency: the currency on a particular bill or receipt.
Fee credit: a separate reduction of an unpaid charge. Student credit: money received but not yet applied. Refund: money returned from unused credit.
For product help, contact support@streaktechnologies.com, +230 215 2998, or visit streaktechnologies.com.
